name: Ursa Minor Dwarf
tagline: A Milky Way spheroid 225,000 light-years out — ancient, faint, and nearly all dark matter.
history: Ursa Minor surfaced on the first Palomar Sky Survey plates in 1955 — the prototype 'fossil' dwarf, its stars uniformly old and metal-poor, suggesting it formed nearly all of them in the first couple billion years and has been passive ever since. Its extreme mass-to-light ratio made it an early benchmark for dark-matter studies, and its orbit carries it on a slow, distant path around the Milky Way.
